title: Prefill Inference Adaptive Fallback Controller: stabilize kernel selection during bursty workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We've observed intermittent kernel oscillation during prefill-heavy traffic spikes where the runtime rapidly alternates between FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants. This produces transient latency tails and small but measurable quality/regression blips for a subset of long-context decoder requests. Existing strategies (fixed hysteresis and simple cooldowns) reduce frequency but do not address multi-minute oscillation patterns caused by feedback between warmup success and prober-triggered handoffs.

Goal: Implement an adaptive fallback controller that stabilizes kernel selection during bursty/prefill-dominated workloads, while preserving fast failover to compatible kernels for memory/throughput anomalies. The controller should be conservative for production routes (SLO-sensitive) and more exploratory in staging/local test nodes.

Design summary:
- Oscillation detection: compute a rolling kernel-churn metric (weighted count of kernel switches per minute) and a latency-skew signal (moving stddev of tail latency for the route). Trigger mitigation when churn > threshold AND latency-skew increases above baseline.
- Controller algorithm: PID-inspired dampener with two control levers: 1) increase preferred-kernel-hold time (backoff multiplier) and 2) suppress prober activation probability (fractional gating). The controller keeps a compact per-route state: last-stable-kernel, hold-until-timestamp, and prober-suppression-factor.
- Prefill-quality guard: before increasing suppression, run a lightweight internal prompt set (5 short prompts) against the candidate kernel in a sandbox to ensure no immediate quality regression. If perplexity/embedding-similarity deviates beyond soft thresholds, allow prober to run (fail open for correctness).
- Telemetry & alerts: emit kernel_churn, controller_state, suppression_factor, and internal-eval-deltas. Add SLO alerting rule for suppression_factor > 0.8 for >5m (signals over-aggressive suppression).
- Rollout plan: small canary on staging->canary fleet with 5% of production routes; monitor latency p50/p95/p99, kernel switch rate, and internal-eval deltas for regressions. Gradual scale and fallback rollback on negative signal.

Tasks:
1) Runtime changes: implement controller hook in kernel-orchestrator, expose per-route hold/suppression config and reconcile loop. (ENG)
2) Telemetry: add kernel_churn and controller telemetry to trace events + metrics. (ENG + Observability)
3) Eval harness: add lightweight internal eval runner invoked by controller sandbox. (Research/Applied ML)
4) E2E canary: integrate into canary rollout pipeline, dashboards, and alerting. (SRE/Product)
5) Testing: load tests with synthetic bursty prefill traffic and offline replay against archived traces. (Performance)

Success criteria: reduced kernel-switch churn by >=70% in synthetic burst tests, no more than 1% regression in internal-eval score across canary routes, and clear reduction in p99 latency tail for affected routes.

Notes on trade-offs: conservative suppression can hide legitimate compatibility regressions; mitigated via prefill-quality guard and explicit canary toggles. We may accept slightly higher median latency for fewer oscillations (depends on route SLO).

Artifacts: Confluence: runtime-attn-stability/Prefill-Fallback-Controller (link forthcoming). GitHub draft PR: github.com/redwood/repro-runtime/pulls/FRONTIER-142 (work-in-progress). Telemetry dashboard: dashboards/redwood/runtime/attn-controller-canary.

Requesting: review of algorithmic thresholds and telemetry schema from Observability and Applied ML; prioritization for an initial 8-point sprint to implement runtime + telemetry hooks.
